prompt: For a conventional exclusive VFIO DPDK application using dedicated always-busy poll loops and no kernel-stack integration, which tradeoffs apply? Select all that apply.

options.text: Polling cores run at 100% CPU even when there's no traffic
options.explanation: Correct. Poll-mode drivers spin on the RX ring instead of sleeping on interrupts.

options.text: The NIC is unbound from the kernel, so `tcpdump`, `ss` and iptables no longer see its traffic
options.explanation: Correct in the stated exclusive data path model: ordinary kernel-stack packet tools do not see that bypassed traffic. The kernel still manages the VFIO device; DPDK-specific capture and other modes can differ.

options.text: You need your own TCP/IP stack if you want TCP on that NIC
options.explanation: Correct. DPDK gives you raw packets; protocol processing is up to you or a user-space stack.

options.text: Every packet still needs a system call to reach user space
options.explanation: DPDK's whole point is the opposite: the process reads the NIC's ring directly, with no syscalls.

workedExample: The stated design avoids ordinary per-packet syscall/skb processing and dedicates CPU polling time. Its bypassed traffic is outside normal kernel-stack tooling, and TCP requires an appropriate TCP/IP stack or integration. DPDK does not universally require these choices: bifurcated drivers, alternative PMDs and power-management modes change the tradeoffs.
